_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.

themes.title: Canada-US trade war live — Sep 29 US import restrictions next binary; Section 338 + Sep 8 retaliation in effect; BoC Oct 28 binary; Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff structural overhang
themes.summary: As of September 27, the Canada-US trade war has added a fresh near-term binary: US import restrictions on Canadian-origin products — described as going 'beyond traditional tariffs' — are scheduled to take effect September 29, per forex.com Q4 2026 outlook data. This escalation sits on top of the existing structural tariff stack: US Section 338 50% tariffs on ~C$27.6 billion of Canadian goods (live since Aug 22), Canada's dollar-for-dollar retaliatory package across 700+ goods lines at 15%, 25%, and 50% (live since Sep 8 at 12:01 a.m.), Trump's federal-contracts ban on Canadian-origin products (unrevoked), and the looming Jan 1, 2027 threat of 50% tariffs on all Canadian autos, trucks, parts, and steel. Zero diplomatic off-ramp remains visible. The Bank of Canada last held at 2.25% on September 2 (seventh consecutive hold) with a mildly hawkish tilt acknowledging inflation risks from tariffs and Middle East energy prices; Canada lost ~42,000 jobs in August with unemployment holding at 6.4%, maintaining the stagflationary dilemma that frames the BoC October 28 binary. Five-bank forecasts place USDCAD at 1.37 in Q4 2026 with upside risk to 1.40-1.41 on further escalation. The oil variable has partially reversed the de-escalation narrative from the prior week: WTI snapped its 5-session losing streak on September 23 when Iran's President Pezeshkian vowed at the UN General Assembly that 'Iran cannot be made to surrender,' pushing WTI to $92.16 (+1.8%) and Brent to $103.08 (+3.9%). By September 25, Brent was at ~$104.5-105.65 as US and Iranian negotiators explored a phased deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but a White House official confirmed Trump sees no pressure to negotiate. WTI was ~$93 on Sep 25. The oil variable is now a two-way binary rather than a clean directional driver: Hormuz deal = oil falls and CAD commodity offset partially restored (USDCAD capped near 1.38-1.39); deal collapse/Iran escalation = oil spikes and CAD partially supported by commodity bid but tariff war headwinds dominate structurally. Net USDCAD directional bias remains bullish on tariff war fundamentals and USD rate advantage, with Sep 29 US import restrictions providing the next near-term catalyst.

themes.title: BOJ hiked to 1.25% Sep 18 (7-2); Oct 28 BOJ next binary at 64% hike odds; Noguchi hawkish; USDJPY pulled back to ~157.18 from 158.37 high; intervention ceiling 160.00 intact; end-Oct dual binary FOMC+BOJ within 48hrs
themes.summary: As of September 27, USDJPY has pulled back from the week-high of 158.365 (Sep 23) to approximately 157.18 by September 25-26, driven by firming BOJ October 28 hike expectations. BBH FX analysts report USDJPY slipped to ~148.50 (note: this appears to be a prior session data point from a different context; confirmed current levels are ~157.18 per TradingEconomics Sep 25 data and Yahoo Finance delayed quote showing 157.185 on the most recent close). The most significant development since Sep 23 is that BOJ board member Asahi Noguchi stated that 'the need to raise rates is increasing more than ever,' a materially hawkish signal that pushed October 28 BOJ hike probability to 64% per BBH's base case and elevated TONA futures pricing. Former BOJ board member Makoto Sakurai separately indicated the BOJ is expected to raise rates roughly once every three months, potentially lifting the policy rate to 2% by around June 2027 — a meaningfully more aggressive normalization path than the market had priced. The Sep 18 hike to 1.25% was the sixth rate increase since exiting NIRP in March 2024 and the highest rate since 1995; the 7-2 vote split (Takata and Tamura dissenting in favor of the hike — actually two dissenters favored a larger or faster hike per BBH) remains a near-term JPY headwind at the margin per OCBC, but Noguchi's latest hawkish signal has meaningfully shifted the balance. The persistent US-Japan rate differential — Fed at 3.75-4.00% (with ~69-75% Oct 27-28 hike odds) versus BOJ at 1.25% — remains the primary structural USDJPY support, keeping carry trade attractive above 157. The critical end-October dual binary remains: Oct 27-28 FOMC (now ~69-75% hike odds) followed immediately by Oct 28-29 BOJ (64% hike odds per BBH, with Outlook Report). The week of Sep 22-26 saw USDJPY range from 155.585 (Sep 17 low) to 158.365 (Sep 23 high) — a 280-pip weekly range confirming the theme's 30+ pip daily impact filter is clearly met. Finance Minister Katayama noted Trump expressed concerns about yen levels in a meeting with PM Takaichi, reinforcing the MoF intervention risk at 160.00.

implications.JPY: BOJ hiked to 1.25% (7-2) Sep 18 but Ueda non-committal presser caused initial USDJPY push above 157. Now Noguchi's 'need to raise rates is increasing more than ever' has firmed Oct 28 BOJ hike odds to 64% (BBH). Sakurai sees rates at 2% by ~June 2027. USDJPY pulled back from 158.365 to ~157.18 on the hawkish BOJ signals. Rate gap with US (3.75-4.00% vs 1.25% = 250bp, widening if Oct FOMC hikes to 4.25%) keeps carry trade structurally attractive. End-October critical dual binary: Oct 27-28 FOMC (~69-75% hike odds) + Oct 28-29 BOJ (64% hike odds, Outlook Report) within 48 hours = maximum USDJPY and JPY-cross volatility. Hawkish BOJ Outlook Report + delivered hike = USDJPY drops toward 153-155; dovish BOJ hold + hawkish FOMC = USDJPY toward 159-160 and MoF intervention risk maximally tested. Trump flagged yen concerns to PM Takaichi — adds political dimension to intervention calculus.

themes.title: Post-dual-hike regime: FOMC Oct 27-28 now ~69-75% hike odds; DXY dipped to ~99.36 on softer inflation but futures price 4.2% Dec; end-Oct compounded binary FOMC+BOJ within 48hrs; G10 rate divergence dominant
themes.summary: As of September 27, the post-FOMC rate divergence regime has evolved materially in the last four days: the October 27-28 FOMC hike probability has surged from ~54% (Sep 23) to approximately 69% (centralbank.watch) to 75.8% (CME FedWatch as of Sep 25), making it a near-consensus live binary rather than a coin-flip. Futures markets as of September 25 are pricing the fed funds rate at approximately 4.2% by December and ~4.8% by September 2027. The Sep 16 dot plot showed four policymakers expecting two more 2026 hikes (October and December), with only eight of twelve dots projecting further 2027 tightening. Headline and core PCE for 2026 are projected at 3.7% and 3.4% respectively, with GDP at 2.3% — a resilient-growth, sticky-inflation backdrop that keeps Warsh's tightening bias institutionally intact. The DXY, however, dipped to approximately 99.36 this week as Goldman Sachs warned against overly hawkish bets and softer inflation signals reduced urgency marginally; the 10-year UST yield is at 4.676% and the 2-year at ~4.12%. The DXY pullback is a tactical development within the broader USD-bullish regime rather than a structural reversal — futures still price 4.2% by December, and the 10yr at 4.676% remains elevated. The oil variable has partially reversed: WTI snapped its 5-session losing streak at $92.16 on Sep 23 as Iran vowed no surrender at the UN General Assembly; Brent recovered to ~$104.5-105 by Sep 25 as US-Iran phased Hormuz reopening talks were reported. This oil recovery partially restores the inflationary urgency narrative (supporting the hawkish Fed path) while also partially restoring commodity-bloc currency support at the margin — a modestly mixed signal for the USD. The G10 rate divergence map remains structurally USD-bullish: Fed at 3.75-4.00% (hiking, with Oct at ~70-75% odds) vs ECB (hold), RBA (hold), RBNZ (hold), SNB (easing). The critical end-October compounded vol event remains: Oct 27-28 FOMC (now ~70-75% hike odds) immediately followed by Oct 28-29 BOJ (64% hike odds per BBH) — this dual binary within 48 hours is the single largest near-term event risk for USDJPY, JPY crosses, and broader G10.

implications.USD: Broadly bullish structurally but DXY pulled back to ~99.36 on softer inflation signals and Goldman Sachs hawkish-bet warning. Fed at 3.75-4.00% (Sep 16, 12-0), Oct 27-28 FOMC now ~69-75.8% hike odds per CME/centralbank.watch Sep 25, futures pricing 4.2% by December and 4.8% by Sep 2027. Dot plot: 4 members expect Oct+Dec hikes. DXY recovery above 100.50 = Oct hike re-priced; pullback sustained below 99.00 = October hike doubts building.

End-October is the critical dual binary within 48 hours. DXY pullback to 99.36 temporarily eases USDJPY upside; Noguchi BOJ hawkish signal offsets. Intervention ceiling at 160.00 intact.

Oil recovery to $93-105 Brent range partially restores CAD commodity offset. BoC Oct 28 binary adds additional CAD directional catalyst.

themes.watchLevel: DXY at ~99.36 (Sep 25 close) — pulled back from ~100.6 (Sep 23) on Goldman Sachs hawkish-bet warning and softer inflation signals. 10yr UST at 4.676%; 2yr at ~4.12%. DXY: recovery above 100.00-100.50 = Oct hike confidence restored and USD bulls re-engage; sustained break below 99.00 = October hike odds declining, USD gives back gains. 10yr UST: sustained above 4.80% = Oct+Dec hike fully priced; pullback below 4.50% = hike doubt. EURUSD: 1.1360 immediate support; break opens 1.1240; bounce above 1.1450 = Oct hike doubt/risk-off. Critical data calendar: Oct 27-28 FOMC is the primary binary (~70-75% hike odds, up from 54% four days ago) — a delivered Oct hike (to 4.25%) front-runs December and accelerates DXY toward 101-102; a surprise hold at Oct reinforces December as last binary and triggers USD give-back. US September PCE (early Oct), September CPI (mid-Oct), and October payrolls (early Nov) are the key inputs before the meeting. Oil wildcard: Brent above $110 (Iran escalation resumes, Hormuz closure) = inflation urgency returns, Oct/Dec hike stays firmly priced; Brent falling below $90 (Hormuz deal fully implemented) = inflation fears ease, Oct/Dec hike odds may slip. End-October compounded vol event: Oct 27-28 FOMC + Oct 28-29 BOJ within 48 hours = maximum USDJPY and JPY-cross volatility. Theme retires: December FOMC decision resolves the primary binary; or 3+ consecutive months of soft CPI/PCE pushing both Oct and Dec hike odds below 30%.
